what: The conversion layer: mechanics proven in high-frequency consumer apps, turned into moves for ads, email, pages and customer portals, each with its evidence and the checks it must pass.
source: Research page of 2 Nov 2026 on betting products and retail use of the same mechanics, with published studies and rule texts. Numbers below are as published; a figure marked second-hand was not read at its origin.
rule: Borrow the mechanic, never the bet. The customer always receives what they paid for, and no money is ever at risk on chance. Each mechanic serves the outcome the customer came for: it shows them getting closer, gives a true reason to act now, or recognizes what they have done.
use: One asset, one lead mechanic, because one clear point gets the response. A second may support it. More than two is a defect.
Pick measured mechanics first. An unproven mechanic runs as a test with a holdout, read on its metric, and is promoted or cut on the numbers.
Every mechanic names the number it moves: cost per click, cost per conversion, order value, upsell take rate, subscription rate, repeat rate or email revenue.
Every fact a mechanic shows (a count, a deadline, a stock level, a price, a tier) comes from live data. An unfilled fact drops the mechanic; it is never estimated.
Every asset passes every gate below. A failed gate is fixed before the asset moves on.

tiers.lab: Effect measured in a lab, survey or hypothetical choice. Direction only.
tiers.unproven: No published number found. Runs only as a test with a holdout.

mechanics.name: Visible progress
mechanics.does: Show how close the customer is to the outcome or reward; effort speeds up as the goal nears.
mechanics.evidence: Time between purchases fell 20% near the reward, 949 cards (Kivetz 2006).
mechanics.ad: Show the journey as a track: day 1, day 14, day 30.
mechanics.email: State where they are on the track and the one next step.
mechanics.page: Show a progress line through the routine or the offer build.
mechanics.portal: A live tracker on the home screen, updated by their own check-ins.

mechanics.name: Head start
mechanics.does: Start the customer partway along instead of at zero.
mechanics.evidence: Redeemed 34% vs 19%, 300 cards (Nunes and Dreze 2006, figures second-hand). Finished in 12.7 vs 15.6 days, N=108 (Kivetz 2006).
mechanics.email: Tell a new buyer the credit already on their track.
mechanics.page: Open the reward bar part-filled after the first add to cart.
mechanics.portal: Credit the first steps at sign-up.

mechanics.name: Real scarcity
mechanics.does: A true limit on supply raises perceived value and speeds purchase.
mechanics.evidence: Purchase intent d=0.31, 193 effects, mostly hypothetical (Barton 2022). Low-stock message: hourly sales +13.6%, returns +17%, net sales +12.5%, matched not randomised (Calvo 2020).
mechanics.ad: Name the true size of the run.
mechanics.email: State units left from live stock.
mechanics.page: Show the live count beside the button.
mechanics.portal: Hold a member's allocation and show what remains.

mechanics.name: Routine streak
mechanics.does: Count consecutive days and protect the streak from one missed day.
mechanics.evidence: Streak protection +0.38% daily actives; separating streak from daily goal +3.3% day-14 retention, company-reported (2020, 2022).
mechanics.email: Send a save message on the day the streak is at risk.
mechanics.portal: Streak count, with a saved day earned by use.

mechanics.name: Triggered message
mechanics.does: Direct messages drive spend, so send them on the customer's own moment instead of the calendar.
mechanics.evidence: Removing all direct marketing for 14 days: bets -23%, spend -39%, N=227 (2026). Whole stream, not one message type.
mechanics.email: Trigger on day of routine, run-out date, tier change and viewed drop.
mechanics.page: Offer the reminder at the point of interest.
mechanics.portal: One alert per real event; the customer sets the volume.

mechanics.name: Risk reversal
mechanics.does: Frame the offer as protected. Among offers tested, money-back had the strongest effect.
mechanics.evidence: Offers raised spend over 10%, money-back strongest, 622 men (ESRI 2025). Loss aversion about 2 to 1, mean 1.955 across 607 estimates (2024), second-hand.
mechanics.ad: Lead with the guarantee as the reason to try.
mechanics.email: Answer the flinch with the guarantee, in plain terms.
mechanics.page: Put the guarantee directly under the button.
mechanics.portal: Show the guarantee window and the day it ends.

mechanics.name: Top customers served first
mechanics.does: A small share of accounts produces most revenue, so identify and serve them directly.
mechanics.evidence: Top 5% by losses gave at least 70% of revenue, 139,152 accounts (UK, 2018-19). US figures unaudited.
mechanics.ad: Build lookalikes from the top tier.
mechanics.email: Personal note and first access to the top tier.
mechanics.page: A members-only door for the top tier.
mechanics.portal: A named contact and early allocation at the top tier.

mechanics.name: Plain value
mechanics.does: Show the result in plain terms. Unfamiliar notation hides what is on offer.
mechanics.evidence: With unfamiliar odds notation, people guessed 53% on a 4% chance, 4,000+, hypothetical (2025).
mechanics.ad: One number the viewer can check in their head.
mechanics.email: Price per day and what is in the box.
mechanics.page: Total, saving and what ships, always beside the button.
mechanics.portal: Plain status: what they have, what they earned, what is next.

mechanics.name: Earned status
mechanics.does: A rank earned and shown makes the top feel higher, more so when a tier sits below it.
mechanics.evidence: Superiority 7.09 vs 5.81 with a tier below, scenario study; feeling special 82% vs 53% for a 1% vs 25% program, n=548 (Dreze and Nunes 2009). No spend number.
mechanics.ad: Speak to the rank by name.
mechanics.email: Announce a rank change as an event.
mechanics.page: Show the tier and what it unlocks.
mechanics.portal: Tier ladder on the home screen, with the next unlock.

mechanics.name: Others shown
mechanics.does: A count of what others chose changes what people choose.
mechanics.evidence: Songs, N=14,341: all social worlds more unequal than independent (2006). Purchase effect not measured.
mechanics.email: Live count of members on the drop.
mechanics.page: Live count of orders and real reviews beside the button.
mechanics.portal: See what people in the same situation use.

mechanics.name: True deadline
mechanics.does: A real end date gives a reason to act now. A timer alone showed no lift.
mechanics.evidence: 60-second timer plus low-stock line 14.3% vs 14.8% control, p=.78 (2021). No randomised field test of a timer alone found.
mechanics.ad: State the date the offer ends.
mechanics.email: One reminder on the last day, stated as a fact.
mechanics.page: Show the end date; a clock only when the offer truly ends at zero.
mechanics.portal: Member window with its real close.

mechanics.name: Surprise reward
mechanics.does: A reward that arrives unpredictably holds attention better than a fixed one.
mechanics.evidence: Dopamine rose on a variable schedule, fixed gave modest increases (2004). Spend not measured.
mechanics.email: An unannounced gift note to a set everyone in that set receives.
mechanics.page: Reveal the free gift after purchase; everyone in the offer gets the same item.
mechanics.portal: Unannounced thank-you credit, given by behaviour.

mechanics.name: First access
mechanics.does: Members buy before the public. Retail uses it widely; no peer-reviewed number exists.
mechanics.evidence: No peer-reviewed number. Vendor figures only.
mechanics.ad: Drive sign-ups to the list before the drop.
mechanics.email: Member door opens first, with the real public date.
mechanics.page: List page before the drop, gated member door during it.
mechanics.portal: The store opens to members first.

mechanics.name: Matched build
mechanics.does: Build the set from the customer's own situation and outcome instead of a catalog.
mechanics.evidence: No published number for matched sets.
mechanics.ad: Name the situation, send to the matcher.
mechanics.email: The set for their stated situation, by name.
mechanics.page: Three questions, then one set, with why each item is in it.
mechanics.portal: The storefront opens on their set, not the catalog.

mechanics.name: Bundle earns more
mechanics.does: Earn rate rises with the size of the set.
mechanics.evidence: Used by large apps in their reward rules. No published behaviour number.
mechanics.email: State the points the full set earns.
mechanics.page: Show points earned changing as items are added.
mechanics.portal: Show earn rate on each set.

mechanics.name: The win moment
mechanics.does: Mark the moment the customer succeeds, and make it shareable.
mechanics.evidence: Widely used in drop apps. No published number.
mechanics.page: Order confirmation as a moment, with the next step.
mechanics.portal: Milestone card with before and after they can share by choice.

mechanics.name: Share the build
mechanics.does: Let customers send their set to a friend, who adds it in one tap.
mechanics.evidence: Shipped by a leading app in 2026. No published effect.
mechanics.email: One link to pass the set to a friend.
mechanics.page: Share button that opens the same set.
mechanics.portal: Send the set, track credits from it.

mechanics.name: Live moment
mechanics.does: A scheduled live event gathers attention and buying at one time.
mechanics.evidence: A leading live platform reports 80 minutes a day and $8B+ sales (2025, company figures). No conversion lift published.
mechanics.email: Reminder at the start of the event.

gates.ask: Is a prize picked by chance tied to a purchase?
gates.pass: No. Everyone in the offer gets the same item, or free entry has equal chance at the same prizes.
gates.basis: Lottery test: prize, chance, consideration. 18 U.S.C. 1302; People v. Miller (N.Y. 1936).

gates.ask: Does a chance promotion carry over $5,000 in prizes?
gates.pass: No, or filed and bonded before start. Thirty days in New York, seven in Florida.

gates.ask: Does every count, stock level, member number and rank come from live data?
gates.basis: 16 CFR 465.8 fake social-influence indicators; FTC Act section 5.

gates.ask: Does the offer truly end or sell out as stated, with no reset?
gates.basis: FTC dark patterns staff report, 15 Sep 2022; NY AG Fareportal.

gates.ask: Is any former price one regularly offered, and is the shown price what is paid?
Are reviews and customer stories real, with paid or given connections disclosed, and rewards not tied to sentiment?
Is every result claim backed by evidence, within cosmetic wording, with typical results disclosed?
gates.basis: 16 CFR 255.2; FTC health claims guidance, Dec 2022; intended-use test.

gates.ask: Does the guarantee state exactly what comes back and how?
gates.pass: Yes, and the word risk-free is not used.
gates.basis: NY AG consumer alert, 10 Feb 2022; state betting rules on the same word.

gates.ask: Are recurring terms stated before purchase, with express consent and a simple way to stop?
Did the customer opt in to this channel, with stop honored?
gates.basis: TCPA for texts; platform sending rules.

gates.ask: For paid social and social shops, does the asset avoid spins, wheels, raffles and sweepstakes, before-and-after comparison where barred, statements of physical inferiority, and implied personal attributes?
gates.basis: Current ad and shop policies, read on the day of launch.
